source: Radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays are all light, with different wavelengths.
Students think radio waves are a kind of sound, or that only visible light is light.

Visible light is a wave too, but it needs no medium: it is a wave of electric and magnetic fields, and it crosses empty space at $300{,}000$ km/s. Visible light is only a thin slice of a much larger family. Every member obeys the same wave equation $v = f\lambda$, all with the same speed in space.

The electromagnetic spectrum, from longest wavelength to shortest: radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light (red to violet), ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays. All of them are light, and all travel at about $3 \times 10^8$ m/s in empty space.

Since every kind travels at the same speed $c$, the equation $c = f\lambda$ means a longer wavelength comes with a lower frequency. Radio waves can be longer than a building, with low frequencies; gamma rays are smaller than an atom, with enormous frequencies. Visible light runs from about 700 nm (red) to about 400 nm (violet), where 1 nm is a billionth of a meter.
The electromagnetic spectrum on a scale where each step is ten times the last. Drag the marker to see a wavelength's band, frequency and photon energy.
Put these in order from longest to shortest wavelength: X-rays, radio waves, visible light, microwaves.

So: radio waves, microwaves, visible light, X-rays.
The Moon is about 384,000 km away. Light travels at about 300,000 km/s. How long does moonlight take to reach us?

Thinking radio waves are a kind of sound, or that only visible light is "light." Radio waves are electromagnetic waves, like light, that travel through space at the speed of light; a radio turns them into sound only at the end. Sound itself can't cross empty space at all.
